lesson.lesson_summary: A review of the noun mistakes learners make most often, one kind per page, each with a correction: -s on uncountable nouns, counting news and advice, wrong irregular plurals, 'one of my friend', two-part nouns, apostrophes in plain plurals, misplaced possessive apostrophes and missing capitals on proper nouns. The rules themselves were taught earlier in this chapter.

success_criteria: Count news and advice with 'a piece of'.
Use irregular plurals such as children and mice.
Use a plural noun after 'one of'.

learning_objectives.description: Correct apostrophe and capital-letter mistakes with nouns.

pages.title: Spot and Fix Noun Mistakes

content.text: Even careful writers slip up with nouns. This lesson collects the most common noun mistakes and shows how to fix each one.

pages.key_takeaway: Most noun mistakes fall into a few groups.

pages.title: No -s on Uncountable Nouns

mistake.incorrect: The guide gave us useful informations.
mistake.correct: The guide gave us useful information.
mistake.reason: Information is uncountable, so it never takes -s.

pages.key_takeaway: Never add -s to an uncountable noun.

pages.title: Counting News and Advice

content.text: Don't put a or a number straight before an uncountable noun. Use a unit word such as a piece of.

mistake.incorrect: She shared a good news with us.
mistake.correct: She shared a good piece of news with us.
mistake.reason: News is uncountable. Count it with a piece of, or say some good news.

pages.key_takeaway: Count news and advice with a piece of.

pages.title: Irregular Plurals, Not -s

mistake.incorrect: Three childs splashed in the puddle.
mistake.correct: Three children splashed in the puddle.
mistake.reason: Child has an irregular plural: children.

content.title: Also
content.text: mice, not mouses; teeth, not tooths; feet, not foots.

pages.key_takeaway: Irregular nouns keep their own plural forms.

pages.title: One of My Friends

content.text: One of means one person or thing from a group, so the noun after it must be plural.

mistake.incorrect: Raju is one of my best friend.
mistake.correct: Raju is one of my best friends.
mistake.reason: Raju is one from a group of friends, so friends is plural.

pages.key_takeaway: After one of, use a plural noun.

pages.title: Two-Part Nouns Stay Plural

mistake.incorrect: I need a scissor for this card.
mistake.correct: I need a pair of scissors for this card.
mistake.reason: Scissors is always plural. Count one item with a pair of.

pages.key_takeaway: Say a pair of scissors, not a scissor.

pages.title: No Apostrophe in Plain Plurals

mistake.reason: Bananas is a plain plural. It owns nothing, so it needs no apostrophe.

pages.key_takeaway: Plain plurals never need an apostrophe.

pages.title: The Apostrophe Follows the Owner

content.text: Put the apostrophe right after the owner word: before the s for one owner, after the s for plural owners ending in s.

mistake.incorrect: All the teacher's cars were parked outside.
mistake.correct: All the teachers' cars were parked outside.
mistake.reason: Many teachers own the cars, so the apostrophe goes after the s.

pages.key_takeaway: Place the apostrophe right after the owner word.

pages.title: Capital Letters for Names

mistake.incorrect: Our school trip to mysore is on friday.
mistake.correct: Our school trip to Mysore is on Friday.
mistake.reason: Mysore and Friday are proper nouns, so they need capital letters.

pages.key_takeaway: Names of places and days need capitals.

pages.title: Noun Mistake Checklist

items: No -s on uncountable nouns: information, advice.
Count news and advice with a piece of.
After one of, a plural noun.
Two-part nouns: a pair of scissors.
No apostrophe in plain plurals; capitals for names.

pages.key_takeaway: Check your nouns before you finish writing.

options.text: We bought new furniture for the flat.
We bought new furnitures for the flat.
We bought a new furnitures for the flat.

question_bank.explanation: Furniture is uncountable, so it never takes -s.

question_bank.prompt: Correct the noun mistake in this sentence.
question_bank.original_sentence: My uncle gave me two advices.
question_bank.corrected_sentence: My uncle gave me two pieces of advice.
accepted_corrections: My uncle gave me some advice.
My uncle gave me two bits of advice.
question_bank.explanation: Advice is uncountable, so we count it in pieces: two pieces of advice.

question_bank.prompt: 'A piece of news' is a correct way to count news.
question_bank.explanation: News is uncountable, so a unit word such as a piece of is needed to count it.

question_bank.prompt: Correct the plural in this sentence.
question_bank.original_sentence: Two mouses ran across the kitchen.
question_bank.corrected_sentence: Two mice ran across the kitchen.
question_bank.explanation: Mouse has an irregular plural: mice.

options.text: Ayesha is one of my cousins.
Ayesha is one of my cousin.
Ayesha is one my cousins.

question_bank.explanation: After one of, the noun must be plural: one of my cousins.

options.text: Pass me the pliers, please.
Pass me the plier, please.
Pass me a plier, please.

question_bank.explanation: Pliers is a two-part tool, so the noun is always plural.

options.text: Cold drinks sold here
Cold drink's sold here
Cold drinks' sold here

question_bank.explanation: Drinks is a plain plural that owns nothing, so it has no apostrophe.

options.text: Ten families' houses were flooded.
Ten family's houses were flooded.
Ten families houses were flooded.

question_bank.explanation: Ten families own the houses. Families ends in s, so the apostrophe goes after the s.

question_bank.prompt: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?

options.text: We flew to Dubai on Tuesday.
We flew to dubai on Tuesday.
We flew to Dubai on tuesday.

question_bank.explanation: Dubai and Tuesday are proper nouns, so both need capitals.

question_bank.prompt: Correct the noun mistake in this sentence.
question_bank.original_sentence: We carried our luggages to the bus.
question_bank.corrected_sentence: We carried our luggage to the bus.
question_bank.explanation: Luggage is uncountable, so it has no -s.

options.text: Both my feet were cold.
Both my foots were cold.
Both my feets were cold.

question_bank.explanation: Foot has an irregular plural, feet, with no -s.

question_bank.original_sentence: This is one of my favourite song.
question_bank.corrected_sentence: This is one of my favourite songs.
question_bank.explanation: After one of, the noun must be plural: songs.

options.text: The stall sells kites and balloons.
The stall sells kite's and balloon's.
The stall sells kites' and balloons'.

question_bank.explanation: Kites and balloons are plain plurals that own nothing, so they need no apostrophes.

question_bank.prompt: Which sentence has no noun mistakes?

options.text: Our teacher gave us some useful advice on Monday.
Our teacher gave us some useful advices on Monday.
Our teacher gave us some useful advice on monday.

question_bank.explanation: Advice takes no -s, and Monday is a proper noun that needs a capital.
